Hi Connor / Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we prepare procurement, Legal at CureLytics flagged two items we need explicit commitments on before we can proceed:

1) A clear "no-training / no model improvement" commitment for customer inputs (both prompts and responses) that includes operational evidence (subprocessor list, retention windows, KMS residency).
2) Confirmation of prompt/response ownership and a proposed output entitlements clause (we want explicit exportability / IP assurances for generated outputs used in our product).

I've attached our redline (CureLytics_DPA_redline_v3.docx) and a short checklist. Can you confirm Redwood can provide an evidence pack we can share with our privacy team (subprocessor inventory, SOC2 logs, onshore KMS options, and a short ops runbook for proof-of-non-training)?

We would prefer a one-page operational summary + the legal redline to move quickly. Also please indicate whether any subprocessor changes would require notice and whether you can guarantee no adaptive training on our data (including derivative use by downstream models).

Looking to close this week if possible — can we get a response by EOD Thu PST?

Thanks,

Emma / Connor — looping in a short legal/ops view.

We reviewed CureLytics' redline. High level: Redwood can accept an explicit prohibition on using customer-provided content for model training or adaptive updates (we'll add defined terms: "Customer Content" and "No Adaptive Training"). Operationally we will:
- Produce a current subprocessor inventory (with regions) and commit to notifying customers 30 days before adding any new subprocessor that processes Customer Content.
- Provide KMS options (customer-managed KMS in US regions and HSM-based KMS for enterprise contracts).
- Provide retention windows and export controls (30/90/365 day retention options depending on plan); we'll include an ephemeral-KV configuration for sensitive workloads.

We recommend adding two contract clauses: one that explicitly states "Redwood will not use Customer Content to improve models or train models" and a second narrow clause granting the customer an irrevocable license to outputs they collect/bring into their product. We can't broadly license derivative works of Redwood's base models, but we can provide output export rights and a warranty that no customer inputs were used to further train Redwood models.

I've attached a short evidence checklist and inline comments to your redline — see attached: no-train-evidence-checklist.pdf and an internal redline (we'll track changes in the DocuSign addendum).

Connor — David will need to confirm operational proof points (logs, runbook, how we isolate KV caches). David, can you drop the ops summary by EOD Thu so we can finalize the addendum?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: No-training assurance + DPA redline — Ops evidence pack

Emma / Kimberly / Connor — operational reply from Privacy & Ops.

Attached is a concise ops summary that addresses CureLytics' ask. Key points:
- Data isolation: Customer inputs are tagged and stored in tenant-scoped buckets. We maintain immutable tenant IDs, and any KV cache used for low-latency sessions is ephemeral by default and can be configured to be ephemeral-only for your account.
- Training ban proof: We keep an audit trail of training data sources. For accounts with a contractual no-training clause, we create a training-exclusion tag that filters data from any internal model-training pipelines. We can produce a nonce-signed snapshot of repository filters on request for due diligence.
- Subprocessors: current list attached (will provide full inventory in the DocuSign package). We will provide 30-day notice for additions that process Customer Content.
- KMS & residency: We support customer-managed keys in US regions (BYOK via AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault), and can pair that with onshore-only processing in our US Dedicated region for added assurance.
- Logs & evidence: We can share SOC2 audit pages, a redacted sample of access logs, and the ops runbook summary for the no-train proof-of-execution.

One caveat on outputs: once Redwood's service returns generated content to a customer, the customer controls that output. We cannot grant the customer ownership of Redwood's underlying model weights or pre-existing model derivatives. Our proposed contract language makes that distinction explicit.

I uploaded the detailed ops pack and a draft addendum to the shared drive and created a DocuSign addendum for signature: https://docusign.com/agree/0a1b2c3d4e5f

I'll be on the Thu 3pm PST call to walk through the evidence pack.

Thanks,
David Kim

Redwood Inference
